contexts.text: The last age is called iron and clay.
The feet of the statue () = lower things which are natural, of which the truths are signified by iron, and the goods by clay, or mire.
The feet which were of iron and clay represented the fourth state, which was one of natural truth, which is iron, and also one of no coherence with good, which is clay.
To which they added a clay age.
Clay () = falsity, which does not cohere with truth and good.
As the last state was the truth which is called of faith, without good, it is said that the feet were partly of iron, and partly of clay.
Such goods as are mentioned above (the good of merit, good for the sake of self and of the world) are signified by clay, or mire.
(The Spirits of the age of iron and clay visited).
(Argument of the predestinarians from the clay of the potter.)

By the feet which were of iron and of clay, is meant the last state of the Church, when there are truth and falsity; truth in the Word and falsity in doctrine. When the truths of the Word are falsified, and doctrine is made from things falsified, the state of the Church is partly iron and partly clay... That thus truths are mixed with falsities, but still do not cohere, is meant by thou sawest iron mixed with clay of mire; they shall mingle themselves together by the seed of man, but they shall not cohere one with another, like as iron is not commingled with clay.
The clay of the potter = the falsities which are in the natural man.
Clay of mire = the falsity which is from man's Own intelligence.
Clay of mire = natural good; but here, clay = good adulterated.
